snippet.description:
Predicting molecular shapes by AB type is a fundamental concept in Class 11 Chemistry Chapter 3. This video explains how to use the AB type notation system to determine the three-dimensional structure of molecules based on the number of atoms bonded to a central atom and lone pairs of electrons.

In this lesson, you'll learn:
• What the AB type notation means and how to apply it
• How to identify central atoms and count bonding pairs
• Methods to predict molecular geometry from electron arrangement
• Common molecular shapes (linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral, trigonal bipyramidal, octahedral)
• Why molecular shape matters in chemistry
• Practice examples following FBISE and PCTB curriculum standards

Understanding molecular shape prediction by AB type is essential for Intermediate (FSc) students preparing for board exams across Federal Board (FBISE), Punjab boards (BISE Lahore, Rawalpindi, Multan, Faisalabad), Sindh boards, KPK, Balochistan, and AJK boards. This concept connects to VSEPR theory and helps explain chemical bonding, reactivity, and molecular polarity.

Whether you're studying for your annual exams, preparing for competitive entry tests, or need extra chemistry help, this step-by-step guide makes shape prediction easy and engaging. Perfect for students, parents supporting their learning, and teachers seeking classroom resources.

Watch, understand, and master predicting molecular shapes. Don't forget to like, subscribe, and comment with any questions!
